text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Parliament rejected the amendments to the anti-corruption law which would have made it legal for deputies, cabinet ministers and civil servants to hold posts in private sector companies. Parliamentary chairman Alfreds Chepanis said he will introduce the amendments again.

- Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs is on a three-day visit in Washington, where he met U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.They discussed the preliminary process of the U.S.- Baltic Charter, the progress of the Baltic Action plan, and co-operation between Latvia and the U.S.

- The three Baltic prime ministers meet in Tallinn today to discuss the proposed customs union and a common market with a focus on the free movement of labour. The prime ministers also plan to sign a joint declaration on their countries' readiness to join the EU.

- The general director of the Latvian Privatisation Agency, Janis Naglis, said that the state's stake in several large enterprises could be sold abroad, possibly through the form of global depository receipts.
- Parekss Bank's profit for the first five months of 1997 amounted to 3.01 million lats. The assets of the bank increased by 7.94 million lats and came to 198.22 million lats.
